caption:
Flight at 6 am and you haven't packed? Tell AI about the trip and ask for a packing list sorted by room, so you walk through your place once.

WHY IT WORKS: a normal list makes you run back and forth. Sorting it by where things live (bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, front door) turns it into one walk. And because AI works from what you tell it (carry-on only, a wedding, a hike, rain), the list fits this trip instead of every trip.

THE REAL TEST: we made up a trip and asked Claude (Anthropic) on Nov 2, 2026: "My flight is at 6 am tomorrow and I haven't packed. 3 nights in Vancouver, carry-on only. There's a wedding on Saturday (I'm wearing a suit), one day hike, and it'll probably rain. Make me a packing list sorted by room in my apartment (bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, front door) so I only walk through once. Keep it short."
It came back with 4 rooms. A few lines, word for word: "Rain jacket (wear it on the plane)" · "Liquids in a clear bag, 100 ml max each" · "Reusable water bottle (empty for security)" · "ID or passport, wallet, keys".
And the carry-on trick, word for word: "Hiking shoes (wear them on the plane, since they're the bulkiest pair)".

HOW (2 minutes, then one walk):
1. Open ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini.
2. Type the trip: how many nights, the bag you're allowed, the plans and the weather.
3. Ask: "Make me a packing list sorted by room in my apartment so I only walk through once. Keep it short."
4. Walk the rooms in its order and tick each line as it goes in the bag.

THE CATCH: AI doesn't know your airline's rules or what's already in your bag. Check your airline's carry-on size and liquids rules before you go, and add anything personal it couldn't guess (glasses, contacts, chargers you always forget).

PRIVACY TIP: "Vancouver, 3 nights" is enough. Leave out your flight number, hotel and home address.

Do this: Ask for a packing list sorted by room.

Send this to whoever always packs at midnight.
